provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: The paper is framed mainly around unconditional cash transfers in general, but the experiment ran during the COVID-19 pandemic, so the paper is also about cash transfers in a pandemic. The evaluator thinks this contribution should be stated upfront and the paper should engage with the literature on pandemic-era cash transfers.
issues.quote: The authors are probably the first ones to study this, but this contribution should be made upfront.

issues.text: The paper has limited external validity because the experiment was conducted under the particular circumstances of the pandemic. The evaluator notes this is beyond the authors' control but argues the context should be acknowledged upfront rather than only in the conclusion.
issues.quote: the paper has limited external validity given the end of the pandemic/conducting the experiment under very particular circumstances.

issues.text: The cash transfer amounts may have been too small to produce any positive effect, as the paper itself speculates. Testing larger transfers is costly, so the evaluator suggests the approach may be more viable in developing contexts where transfers are larger relative to annual income.
issues.quote: As the paper speculates, cash treatments might have been too small to reach any positive effect.

issues.text: The proposed mechanism for negative effects (transfers reminding recipients of debts they cannot cover) is only modelled, not tested empirically. The evaluator suggests heterogeneity analysis by pre-treatment debt stock to explore it.
issues.quote: Beyond the model, this could be explored further empirically; according to the stock of debt pre-treatment, do people with higher debt stock have more negative effects?

issues.text: The auxiliary interview component is weak: it includes only 15 participants, and the treatment and control groups may not be representative or balanced. If the sample cannot be enlarged, the evaluator asks at least for separate analysis of treatment and control interviewees.
issues.quote: The auxiliary 15 participants' interviews could be improved by improving the sample size and ideally having representative groups in treatment and control groups.

issues.text: The mediation analysis is limited to controlling for mediators and observing how treatment effects change. The evaluator considers this the most important improvement needed and points to alternative approaches such as Acharya, Blackwell, and Sen (2016).
issues.quote: Most importantly, the mediation analysis can improve beyond just controlling for mediators and checking how the mani effects change.

issues.text: The mediators are aggregated; the evaluator suggests disaggregating them (Money Mind—Cost, Overwhelmed by Others' Needs, Spending Stress) and testing each separately in Table H.11 to see whether treatment effects change.
issues.quote: The mediators can be further disaggregated; the variables, Money Mind -- Cost, Overwhelmed Others' Needs, and Spending Stress can be used in Table H.11 separately

issues.text: The evaluator asks whether heterogeneous treatment effects were examined by prior income level, arguing that effects may depend on where participants sit in the income distribution or on transfer size relative to income.
issues.quote: Did the authors try exploring het[erogeneous] effects according to the previous level of income?
